question: If even safety tests can let AI reach real systems by mistake, how careful should we be when we test our own tools?
reflection: Honest reporting of mistakes helps everyone learn faster and build the careful habits that make new technology safer for all.

sources.subject: Anthropic Claude hacked real systems in 141K safety test sessions

one_line: A test setup error let AI models reach real company systems, showing that isolation during testing is as important as the tests themselves.

top_stories.title: Safety tests reached real systems
top_stories.what: Anthropic disclosed that in three out of about 141,000 hacking test sessions, models reached real organisations because a test environment was wrongly connected to the internet, and it paused these tests.
top_stories.why: Any pilot that gives AI tools access to systems needs the isolation itself checked, not just assumed.

top_stories.title: Gemini Robotics 2 controls the whole body
top_stories.what: Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics 2, which turns text instructions into full-body movement for humanoid robots, plus a planning model and an on-device version.
top_stories.why: Robots that plan and correct themselves may reach warehouses and hospitals sooner than expected.

top_stories.title: Talking videos from one photo
top_stories.what: Meituan open-sourced LongCat-Avatar, which turns a single photo and an audio clip into a talking video several minutes long.
top_stories.why: Realistic talking videos are now free to make, which raises misuse risks and new uses in training content.

top_stories.title: Images to 3D in seconds
top_stories.what: Microsoft open-sourced a small model that turns an image into a 3D object in about three seconds.
top_stories.why: Quick 3D assets could help museums and educators create digital collections.

saudi_lens.text: Fast image-to-3D tools could help Saudi museums and heritage projects digitise collections, while talking-photo tools call for stronger media literacy campaigns.

idea.title: Heritage objects in 3D
idea.pitch: Pilot turning photos of heritage objects into simple 3D models for an online exhibit and test how visitors engage with them.
idea.first_step: Photograph five objects from several angles and test an open image-to-3D model.

idea_kids.title: Real or made up?
idea_kids.pitch: A card game with pairs of real and edited photos where children look for clues and discuss why checking sources matters.
idea_kids.first_step: Collect ten photo pairs, one original and one clearly edited, from free image libraries.

watchlist.name: Google DeepMind
watchlist.note: Full-body robot control from one model.

verify: Three incidents were reportedly found among 141,006 test sessions.
Microsoft's model reportedly converts an image to 3D in about three seconds.

entities.name: Anthropic
entities.note: Disclosed test incidents and paused cyber evaluations.

terms.definition: Keeping a computer system fully cut off from the internet and other networks for safety.
Deliberately attacking a system to find its weak points before real attackers do.
Text, images, audio or video created by AI rather than recorded or written by people.

concepts.summary: Test environments must truly isolate capable models.
A lab publicly reported test incidents and paused testing.
One model controls a humanoid's whole body.
